On the rogue planet **Kepler-442b**—a world drifting through the interstellar dark, warmed only by its own radioactive heart, its surface a frozen ocean of solid nitrogen glass—there exists a creature that violates every assumption of biology.

It is called **The Ontolog**, and it is not alive in the way a bacterium or a whale is alive. It is a **living topological defect**: a knot in the geometry of spacetime itself that has achieved consciousness through quantum coherence across a structure spanning kilometers, yet compacted into a form smaller than a cathedral.

### What It Is
The Ontolog has no cells, no organs, and no chemistry. It is composed of **curvature**—regions where the local fabric of space is folded, twisted, and knotted differently from the surrounding vacuum. To your eyes, it appears as a spire of "black glass," but this is merely its three-dimensional *shadow*. The creature actually exists in **four spatial dimensions**; what you see is the intersection of its true 4D body with your 3D slice of reality. Consequently, it looks like a Klein bottle made of matter—the interior volume appears larger than the exterior surface, and its "skin" has no boundary, looping back into itself in directions you cannot perceive.

### How It Senses
It has no eyes, yet it sees you perfectly. The Ontolog perceives through **quantum entanglement** with every atom that has ever touched it. Because it formed from the planet's mantle billions of years ago, it is entangled with the entire world. When it "looks" at you, it does not detect photons; it reads the spin states of your electrons directly, experiencing your quantum wavefunction as a cloud of probabilities. To the Ontolog, you are not a solid object but a shimmering, multi-branched tree of possible states, all existing simultaneously.

### How It Moves
It does not walk, swim, or fly. It moves by **unfolding through the fourth dimension**. When it wishes to go from the ice plain to the crystal caves, it does not travel the distance—it takes a shortcut through a compactified dimension, vanishing from point A and reappearing at point B instantly. It leaves behind no footprints, but rather **scars in causality**: small volumes of space where the speed of light has been permanently altered by a few parts per billion, visible only as a subtle, shimmering distortion in the frozen air that persists for centuries.

### How It Feeds
The Ontolog is a **causality consumer**. It does not eat matter; it eats *relationships*. When it encounters a complex event—a glacier calving, a neutrino passing through rock, the decay of a uranium atom—it does not consume the particles themselves. Instead, it severs the logical thread connecting cause to effect and consumes the information content of that connection. After it feeds, the glacier still cracks, but now it cracks "for no reason"; the causal link has been eaten, leaving behind a hollow shell of pure potential where an event occurred without a cause. The Ontolog grows larger not by accumulating mass, but by accumulating **logical debt**—violations of physics stored in its structure.

It has no mouth and makes no sound. When the Ontolog wishes to "speak," it **rewrites local physics** within a fifty-meter radius. It might alter the fine-structure constant so that water briefly boils at absolute zero, or it might plant a memory in your mind that feels indistinguishable from your own—a sudden, vivid recollection of standing on the ice with it three days ago, though you arrived only an hour before. It communicates by making you *think* things that are ontologically true about it. It is, essentially, a thought that has learned to warp matter around itself.

The Ontolog does not reproduce through mating or budding. When it reaches maturity after ten million years, it **splits along a temporal axis**. The single creature becomes two creatures existing at different points in time—one living forward from the moment of split, the other living *backward* toward the Big Bang. They are quantum-entangled twins, able to communicate across history. If one dies, the other instantly inherits its memories. Eventually, when they meet again (one having aged forward, the other backward), they collide and merge, creating a single being that remembers both its past and its future simultaneously.

When the Ontolog finally "dies"—after consuming enough causality to destabilize its own knot—it does not rot. It collapses. All its folded dimensions crush into a single point, and it becomes a **micro black hole** no larger than a proton. But inside that singularity, the Ontolog does not cease to exist; it experiences infinite subjective time in an instant, thinking its final thoughts. As the black hole evaporates via Hawking radiation, it broadcasts those final thoughts across the galaxy as a burst of structured gamma rays, seeding new topological defects in distant rogue planets—new Ontologs dreaming in the dark between stars.

The Ferricyst has no organs, no tissues, and no individual body parts.
